questions.answer: Engine is the long-lived DB connection (created once). Session is a short-lived workspace that tracks adds/queries and flushes on commit; FastAPI creates one per request via a yield dependency and closes it after.
questions.question: Explain Engine vs Session in SQLAlchemy.

questions.answer: One-to-one uses FK with unique=True (user-profile). One-to-many uses parent list + child FK (user-orders). Many-to-many uses an association Table with secondary= (students-courses); use a full model if the link has extra columns.
questions.question: How do you model 1-1, 1-N, and N-N relationships?

questions.answer: Lazy loads relationships on access, causing N+1 queries in loops. Eager loading via selectinload/joinedload fetches them upfront in 1-2 queries. Use eager when you know you need the relation.
questions.question: What is the N+1 problem and how does eager loading fix it?

from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload

user = session.scalars(stmt).first()

questions.answer: create_all blindly creates tables with no history, review, or rollback — fine for dev/tests. Production needs Alembic revisions (autogenerate, review, upgrade head) so schema changes are versioned and reversible.
questions.question: Trap: why not use Base.metadata.create_all() in production?

questions.answer: After a failed commit the session stays in a broken state; continuing without rollback raises PendingRollbackError and can partially persist. Always try/commit except/rollback.
